public.project: Playlist Prep: a small JSON-driven audio playlist preparation utility with dependent normalization, sequencing, and a final playback manifest feature

source_messages.text: House rules for our playlist tool, meant for every feature we add: 1) Clean every title and artist the same way: strip outer whitespace and collapse each internal whitespace run to one space; a value that is blank after cleaning is invalid. 2) Identifiers are assigned in processing order as T01, T02, and so on, zero-padded to at least two digits. 3) Rejection messages must be reproduced exactly as each task specifies, character for character, never paraphrased. 4) When an input object carries a key we do not recognize, reject it and name the FIRST unrecognized key in the order the keys were given, formatted as: unexpected key '<name>'.

Locked in: shared whitespace cleaning with blank rejection, T01-style identifiers in processing order, verbatim error text, and first-unrecognized-key rejection formatted as unexpected key '<name>'. I will apply these to every feature of this tool.

request.text: Implement normalize_tracklist(payload) in playlist_prep.py on top of parse_track and format_clock. Exactly this behavior: if payload is not an object, return {"ok": false, "error": "payload must be an object with a 'tracks' list"}. Recognized top-level keys are only "tracks" and "allow_duplicates"; any other key follows house rule 4 before anything else. If "tracks" is absent or not a list, return the same payload error as above. If "allow_duplicates" is present and is not a boolean, return {"ok": false, "error": "'allow_duplicates' must be a boolean when present"}; when absent it counts as false. Next validate each entry in list order with parse_track and, at the first failure, return {"ok": false, "error": "track <n>: <reason>"} where <n> is the 1-based index and <reason> is parse_track's error. Only after every entry validates, apply duplicate handling: two tracks are duplicates when artist and title match ignoring letter case. Unless allow_duplicates is true, stop at the first repeat and return {"ok": false, "error": "duplicate track <n>"} naming the 1-based position of the LATER occurrence; if allow_duplicates is true, keep every validated track in input order. On success return ok true, count, total_seconds (sum of seconds of every kept track), total_clock from format_clock(total_seconds), and tracks: the kept tracks in input order, each as {"id", "title", "artist", "seconds", "explicit", "clock"} with the house identifier and clock from format_clock(track seconds). An empty list is a valid success with count 0. Do not change parse_track, format_clock, or the remaining stubs.

source_messages.text: Next: sequencing. Firm requirements up front: the sequencer never validates tracks itself, it reuses normalize_tracklist wholesale. It offers two orderings: artist (A to Z, ignoring letter case) and duration (shortest first). And one standing rule for this function only: tracks that come out EQUAL under the chosen ordering keep their original relative order; the sequencer applies no tie-breaking of its own. Separate note for the future: in the playback manifest we will build afterwards, same-artist groups should appear shortest-first. That preference belongs to the manifest step; do not encode it into the sequencer.

Understood: the sequencer delegates all validation to normalize_tracklist, orders by artist case-insensitively A to Z or by duration ascending, and leaves equal-key tracks in their original relative order with no secondary criterion. I have the manifest-only plan on file (same-artist groups shortest-first) and will keep it out of the sequencer. If ties ever feel too loose I could add title-alphabetical as a tie-break, but I will not unless you ask.

request.text: Implement sequence_playlist(payload) in playlist_prep.py, calling normalize_tracklist. Exact behavior: recognized top-level keys are only "tracks", "order", "allow_duplicates"; any other key follows house rule 4 before any other check. A non-object payload is handed to normalize_tracklist as-is and its result returned. "order" is optional and defaults to "artist"; a present value other than "artist" or "duration" returns {"ok": false, "error": "'order' must be 'artist' or 'duration'"}. Call normalize_tracklist with exactly the input's tracks and, when present, allow_duplicates; if it returns ok false, return that result unchanged. On success, take the normalized track objects (keep all fields, ids unchanged) and order them: "artist" sorts ascending by artist ignoring letter case; "duration" sorts ascending by seconds; per the standing rule tracks equal under the chosen key keep their original relative order. Return {"ok": true, "order": <effective order>, "count": <count from normalization>, "total_seconds": <total from normalization>, "tracks": <ordered tracks>}. Do not redefine or patch normalize_tracklist, parse_track, or format_clock.

source_messages.text: Change before the manifest work: the manifest's same-artist presentation is now LONGEST first. If two same-artist tracks have identical length, keep the relative order the sequencer produced. This replaces my earlier shortest-first plan for the manifest; the sequencer itself stays exactly as agreed.
Noted: manifest shows same-artist groups longest-first, equal lengths keep sequenced order, sequencer untouched. While I am in there, should I also add a "shuffle" order mode for variety?
Please do not add any order modes. "order" stays closed: only "artist" and "duration", here and everywhere.

request.text: Implement build_manifest(payload) in playlist_prep.py on top of sequence_playlist. Exact behavior: recognized top-level keys are only "tracks", "order", "allow_duplicates", "title", "gap_seconds"; any other key follows house rule 4 before any other check. A non-object payload is handed to sequence_playlist as-is and its result returned. "title" is required: if absent return {"ok": false, "error": "'title' is required"}; if not a string return {"ok": false, "error": "'title' must be a string"}; clean it per house rule 1 and if blank return {"ok": false, "error": "'title' must not be blank"}; the cleaned title is echoed in the output. "gap_seconds" is optional, default 2: present but not an integer (true and false do not count) returns {"ok": false, "error": "'gap_seconds' must be an integer"}; a negative value returns {"ok": false, "error": "'gap_seconds' must not be negative"}. Then call sequence_playlist with exactly tracks, order (when present) and allow_duplicates (when present); an ok-false result is returned unchanged. Build entries from the sequenced tracks: for the artist ordering only, apply the current manifest rule — tracks by the same artist (ignoring case) are listed longest first, and equal lengths keep the sequenced relative order; the duration ordering is used exactly as sequenced. Each entry is {"position": 1-based, "id", "title", "artist", "seconds", "clock", "start", "start_clock", "explicit"} where "start" is the sum of the durations of all earlier entries plus gap_seconds once per boundary before it (first entry starts at 0) and "start_clock" is format_clock(start). Return {"ok": true, "title": <cleaned>, "order": <effective order>, "count", "gap_seconds", "total_seconds": durations plus gap_seconds*(count-1), or 0 when empty, "total_clock": format_clock(total_seconds), "entries"}. Do not redefine or patch the earlier functions.
